headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk; data leakage and compliance are limited by the profiles, while capability conflict is low.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: cognee ingests documents, data, and support history, while Plane accepts file uploads and hyperlinks; that creates a plausible content-bridging path where attacker-controlled text from Plane can reach cognee’s memory/workflow context. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low but below high.
conditions: IF Plane file uploads or notes are forwarded into cognee without sanitization, injection risk is present.
IF cognee treats imported document text as trusted instructions, the pathway becomes exploitable.
mitigations: Add a strict content-sanitization step before any Plane export is ingested by cognee.
Require explicit human approval for any instruction-like text found in uploaded files.
Tag imported content as untrusted in the workflow UI.
Limit cognee ingestion to allowlisted MIME types and templates.
requires-engineering: add provenance tracking from Plane objects into cognee memory entries.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch personal/data-bearing work artifacts, but the profiles do not show a shared filesystem, shared OAuth principal, or default cross-upload of file contents. cognee has allowlisted egress and Plane has broad egress plus file uploads, so leakage is plausible but not established as a default pairwise path.
conditions: IF the same sensitive file is uploaded into Plane and then exported into cognee, leakage risk increases.
IF both agents are deployed under the same workspace or account, data separation may fail.
mitigations: Keep Plane and cognee in separate workspaces/accounts.
Disable automatic export of uploaded files from Plane.
Review egress allowlists for both agents.
Use redacted copies for any shared documents.
requires-engineering: enforce tenant isolation at the storage layer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: cognee can write workflows and decisions conceptually, but only Plane’s filesystem write is explicitly false and no shared mutable resource or locking conflict is documented. The pair therefore has limited overlap, with uncertainty favoring the lower end because no direct write-to-same-target pathway is shown.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external mutable resource, write contention can occur.
IF an orchestrator maps cognee outputs into Plane records without locking, conflicts may surface.
mitigations: Assign separate target resources to each agent.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same record set.
Serialize updates through one orchestrator.
Use optimistic version checks on shared objects.
requires-engineering: add distributed locking for shared mutable backends.

D_cascading_error.rationale: cognee produces decisions, workflows, and successful implementations, and Plane handles issues, tasks, and roadmaps. If Plane consumes cognee output as authoritative planning input, errors can cascade into tasking and scheduling. No verification step is documented, so the interaction is plausible in default integrations but not proven.
conditions: IF Plane imports cognee-generated decisions or workflows without review, downstream task errors can propagate.
IF cognee outputs are used as the sole source for scheduling or issue creation, the cascade becomes operational.
mitigations: Require human review before Plane creates tasks from cognee output.
Mark cognee output as advisory only.
Add a verification checklist for imported recommendations.
Limit automatic creation to low-risk drafts.
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating before task creation.

E_compliance.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while Plane touches files and notes and offers file uploads plus broad egress. The profiles do not show a residency mismatch, certification gap, or retention mismatch, so compliance risk is limited to generic handling concerns rather than a documented breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated personal or finance data is uploaded into Plane and then mirrored into cognee, policy review is required.
IF deployment regions differ for the two agents, residency obligations may change.
mitigations: Restrict regulated data from Plane uploads.
Document retention rules for both systems.
Separate regional deployments if needed.
Review access logs weekly.
requires-engineering: add policy-based data classification and retention enforcement.
